column1: # A client with ten payrolls has ten SQL Server databases and ten rows here
# against the SAME tenant_slug — payrolls are rows inside one tenant
# separate tenants.
# COLUMNS
#   source_db              the SQL Server database you restore and point
#                          PostgresImport at. Recorded so the log says which
#                          backup produced which schemas; nothing connects to it
#                          from here.
#   company_schema         where this payroll's interim COMPANY schema is parked
#   payroll_schema         ... and its PAYROLL schema
#                          Both must be UNIQUE across the manifest: PostgresImport
#                          always writes the same two schema names on the desktop
#                          so each payroll is renamed on the way into docker or the
#                          next run overwrites the last. Never use 'pipro' for the
#                          payroll one - it shadows 'public' for the app's own user.
#   tenant_slug            target tenant (tenant_<slug>)
#   target_payroll_id      target payrolls.id in that tenant
#   legacy_payroll_number  the interim/legacy Payroll number. VERIFIED against the
#                          data after the refresh
#   role                   current | history
#   tax_year               required for history rows
# role=history is not implemented yet; rows are validated and reported
# skipped. See conversion-plan.md section 5.
source_db
